title: Kernel stability siege testing and metrics manifest
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary:

This document defines the 'siege testing' program for runtime kernel components: a repeatable, low-variability stress protocol designed to exercise kernel hot paths, handoff/fallback logic, allocator behavior, and scheduler admission/signaling. The goal is to produce deterministic signal surfaces and a small set of stable metrics that correlate with production regressions and that can be used as gates for kernel changes and experimental rollouts.

Scope:
- Components: kernel dispatcher, prefetch/hint path, batch slicer, KV cache eviction function, tensor allocator, cooperative preemption shim.
- Environments: synthetic lab cluster (staging-fidelity-1), canary pool, and a shadow-prod replay mode.
- Exclusions: network stack-wide failures, hardware thermal throttling (handled separately).

Why 'siege' testing?
- Traditional microbenchmarks miss cross-component contention; siege runs sustained, controlled contention across shared resources to reveal systemic instabilities (oscillation, runaway backpressure, allocator landlocks).

Testing matrix and workload catalog:

1) Workload classes (representative):
   a) Short-chat burst (seq_len 32, reply tokens 32): high qps, small KV reuse.
   b) Long-completion (seq_len 1024, reply tokens 512): memory-heavy, long kernel occupancy.
   c) Mixed-concurrency (50% short, 25% long, 25% moderate): mimics PLG mixed surface.
   d) Cold-start storm (many first-frame requests with empty caches).
   e) Model-switch churn (frequent model variants and quantization profile swaps).

2) Siege axes (vary these orthogonally):
   - Concurrency (clients): 100, 500, 2000
   - Batch-intent randomness: deterministic vs jittered arrival
   - Kernel variant set: baseline, opt-kernel-A, fallback-emu
   - KV cache hit ratio: 10%, 50%, 90%
   - Quantization mode: fp16, int8-quantized

Metrics manifest (canonical signals) - interpreted as single-line CSV-compatible columns for dashboards:

| metric_name                          | description                                                   | unit    | sampling_window |
|--------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|---------|-----------------|
| kernel_dispatch_latency_p50          | kernel dispatcher processing latency (p50)                    | ms      | 1m              |
| kernel_dispatch_latency_p95          | p95 latency for kernel dispatch                               | ms      | 1m              |
| kernel_dispatch_latency_p99          | p99 (captures microbursts / hitch)                            | ms      | 1m              |
| kernel_cpu_busy_ratio                | % time CPU-bound in kernel control loops                      | pct     | 1m              |
| kernel_gpu_occupancy_ratio           | % GPU occupancy recorded during runs                          | pct     | 1m              |
| allocator_fragmentation_score       | normalized score (0..1) indicating fragmentation severity     | unitless| 5m              |
| kvcache_eviction_rate                | evictions per second                                          | /s     | 1m              |
| backpressure_retry_rate              | fraction of requests retried due to admission                 | pct     | 1m              |
| kernel_fallback_count                | number of fallback activations (kernel -> software-path)      | count   | 1m              |
| input_tail_response_time_p999        | e2e input->final-token latency p999                           | ms      | 1m              |
| kernel_stall_incidents               | counted 10s+ stalls identified by watchdog                     | count   | 1m              |
| error_budget_consumed_rate           | % of configured SLO budget used due to this test              | pct     | 1m              |

Pass / fail and stability criteria:
- Green: All p99 latencies < target for workload class, allocator_fragmentation_score < 0.3, kernel_fallback_count == 0 during steady-state 30m window.
- Amber: Any single metric crosses warning threshold (p99 > target*1.5 or fragmentation > 0.6), or >5 fallback activations in 30m. Requires immediate engineering review and localized bisect.
- Red: Recurring oscillation (latency spikes followed by capacity collapse) or kernel_stall_incidents > 3 in 10m. Block rollout and open P1 triage.

Example thresholds (should be tuned per-model):
- Short-chat: p99 < 120ms (green), warning if >180ms, critical >400ms.
- Long-completion: p99 < 900ms (green), warning if >1400ms, critical >3000ms.

Run procedure (operator-run; 20–60 minutes per configuration):
1) Pre-checks:
   - Ensure staging-fidelity-1 node labels and quotas are provisioned: 
     * kubectl get nodes -l env=staging-fidelity-1
   - Confirm telemetry ingestion: grafana/ingest check 'kernel_dispatch_latency_p95' has fresh datapoints.
2) Deploy test harness (siege-runner):
   - git clone git@internal:redwood/siege-runner.git && cd siege-runner
   - kubectl apply -f deploy/siege-runner-staging.yaml --record
3) Load scenario selection:
   - Edit scenarios/config.yaml: set workload_class, concurrency, kv_hit_target.
   - Example snippet:
     workload: short-chat
     concurrency: 500
     batch_jitter_ms: 5
     kv_hit_ratio: 0.5
4) Start run and tag with experiment metadata:
   - ./bin/siege-runner --scenario scenarios/config.yaml --tags kernel-experiment=stable-2026 --duration 30m
5) Observe live dashboards: grafana dashboard id: runtime-kernel-siege-v2 (owner: eng-serving-runtime)
6) Collect artifacts at end: traces archive (traces.tar.gz), perf profiles (perf.data), allocator heap dumps (allocator-heap-*.bin), and the siege-runner events.json.
7) Upload to artifact store: rclone cp traces.tar.gz remote:kernel-siege/2026-02-03-<runid>

Instrumentation and telemetry guidance:
- Required tracing spans: kernel.dispatch, kernel.batch_slice, allocator.malloc, kvcache.evict, scheduler.admit. Ensure spans include kernel_variant, model_id, request_cohort labels.
- Sampling policy: 100% for p99 tail-trace capture during siege; annotated with 'siege_run_id'.
- Lightweight task-level counters should be emitted at 1s resolution to Prometheus push gateway for short retention.

Dashboards and alerting (deliverables):
- runtime-kernel-siege-v2 (Grafana): combined heatmap of p99 over concurrency sweep, allocator fragmentation trend, fallback waterfall chart.
- Alerts (temporary during siege): alert if kernel_stall_incidents > 1 in 2m or backpressure_retry_rate > 2%.

Analysis checklist (post-run):
1) Verify steady-state window (last 20m) has stable request rates.
2) Correlate p99 spikes with kernel_fallback_count and allocator_fragmentation_score.
3) Inspect traces for sequential blocking patterns (allocator->dispatcher->kvcache).
4) Run deterministic replay of top-5 tail traces with kernel variant toggles.
5) If amber/red observed, run a binary bisect: isolate last change (kernel commit range) and re-run siege with single-commit rollback.

Binary bisect protocol (fast safety bisect):
1) Narrow candidate commits to the minimal set by commit-time ordering and previous green runs.
2) Deploy candidate commit to a 2-node canary pool with identical siege workload.
3) Run 10m micro-siege focused on reproducing failing signal.
4) If failing, mark commit as suspect and iterate; if green, exclude commit and continue.

Artifacts to archive per run (minimum):
- siege-metadata.json (scenario + tags)
- traces.tar.gz (all collected spans)
- perf-summaries.csv (per-node p50/p95/p99)
- allocator-heap-*.bin
- kube-state-dump.yaml

Ownership and cadence:
- Program owner: runtime-reliability (eng-serving-runtime) — primary contact: Asha Patel (author).
- Siege maintenance: rotate workloads quarterly and review thresholds after each major kernel merge.
- Scheduled runs: weekly smoke (short 20m mixed-concurrency) and monthly deep-siege (full matrix).

Runbook: interpreting common failure modes:
- Symptom: p99 spikes + immediate kernel_fallback_count increase. Likely cause: kernel invariant assertion or slow path fallback. Action: check kernel logs (grep "fallback-activated" /var/log/kernel/*.log), collect first-tail trace, disable canary kernel variant.
- Symptom: allocator_fragmentation_score rising steadily with long-completion workloads. Likely cause: allocation patterns + tensor pinning. Action: trigger allocator-compact routine, capture heap dump, run reproducer with slab debugging flags.
- Symptom: oscillation between high occupancy and near-zero throughput. Likely cause: admission controller thresholds too aggressive combined with eviction storm. Action: reduce admission aggression, increase kvcache size for test, re-run.

Security and data handling:
- Siege runs must not use customer data. All test corpora reside in 'siege-corpus/public' and are sanitized.
- Artifacts containing telemetry are internal-only; upload paths are restricted to eng-serving-runtime group.

Appendix: example CLI recipes
- Start a short-chat siege locally (developer):
  ./bin/siege-runner --scenario scenarios/short-chat.yaml --concurrency 100 --duration 20m --local-debug

- Replay a trace against a kernel variant under test:
  ./bin/trace-replay --trace traces/tail-1234.json --kernel-variant opt-kernel-A --replay-speed real-time

Notes and future work:
- Add thermal/NRM (non-replayable memory pressure) axis to catch hardware-coupled flakes.
- Integrate automated bisect with CI as an optional post-merge siege gate for high-risk kernel changes.

References:
- See related: controlled-kernel-perturbation-playbook (link in related_pages).
